headlines.title: ETFs Are Net Sellers of Cisco (CSCO) on Nov. 17
headlines.summary: ETFs sold a net $189.2 million of Cisco stock on Tuesday, Nov. 17.

headlines.title: Gold, Silver and Crude Slide Hard as Volatility Jumps on the Week
headlines.summary: Stock Preachers News Commentary - Major indices were mixed as of midday Wednesday, with the Dow down sharply and the Nasdaq Composite little changed to higher on the day even as all four benchmarks remain lower on the week. Gold, silver and crude oil all fell sharply on the day and the week, while the CBOE Volatility Index eased on the day but jumped on the week. Against that backdrop, cybersecurity and semiconductor-linked names drew attention, led by Cisco's latest quarterly results.

headlines.title: Beyond Static Estimates: How Cisco's Product Carbon Footprint Feature Tracks a Decarbonizing Grid
headlines.summary: NORTHAMPTON, MA / ACCESS Newswire / November 18, 2026 / by Lucy NguyenCiscoBusinesses are setting ambitious net-zero targets while facing increasing demands for transparent, verifiable data on their Scope 3 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. For many, this is where the carbon footprint of purchased products, like Cisco hardware, can become a critical piece of the sustainability puzzle.

headlines.title: Cisco (CSCO) Stock Lags Record Q1 Earnings As AI Revenue Builds
headlines.summary: Cisco Systems just posted Q1 FY2027 numbers that read like a victory lap, while the stock is only inching higher. Shares closed at US$97.18, up 2.2% on the day, even as the networking giant delivered record quarterly revenue of US$18.5b and non GAAP earnings per share of US$1.40. That gap between a modest price move and a very strong earnings print is the story. The market is reacting, but not as dramatically as the fundamentals might suggest.

headlines.title: NVIDIA vs. Cisco: One AI Stock Looks Like a Better Buy Now
headlines.summary: Cisco's stable leadership, diversified revenue streams and raised 2027 outlook could make it a better-balanced investment than NVIDIA amid AI spending concerns.

description: Cisco Systems, Inc. designs, develops, and sells technologies to power, help, secure, and draw insights from the internet in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Asia Pacific, Japan, and China. The company provides data center switching; network security, identity and access management, and secure access service edge; identity and agentic security solutions; interconnects public and private wireline and mobile networks, delivering connectivity to campus, data center, and branch networks; WEBEX suite, collaboration devices, and contact center; communication platform as a service software, including perpetual licenses, subscription arrangements, and hardware solutions; network assurance and observability suite; accelerated issue resolution, software support, and hardware replacement; professional services, such as planning, design, implementation, and high-value consulting; service and support packages, financing, and managed network services; and regional, national, and international wireline carriers, webscale products, internet, and cable. It also provides wireless products, including indoor and outdoor coverage designed for seamless roaming use of voice, video, and data applications; end-to-end collaboration solutions through cloud, on-premise, or within hybrid cloud environments. In addition, it offers technical support services. The company serves businesses, public institutions, governments, and service providers. It sells its products and services directly, through systems integrators, service providers, and resellers, and distributors. It has a collaboration with NVIDIA Corporation to develop Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP), a high-density optical module pluggable transceiver. Cisco Systems, Inc. was incorporated in 1984 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.
